closed.content: Tests in atlas are run through cargo nextest run; plain cargo test is not used.
The atlas test suite is run with cargo nextest run, not cargo test.
Project atlas is deployed by running bin/ship.sh from the repository root.
To ship atlas you run the bin/ship.sh script at the top of the repo.
Deploying atlas means executing bin/ship.sh; the old make deploy target is gone.
The branch under review is spike/consolidate.
The flaky test being chased this week is pagination_ordering in atlas-api.

**Needs your call — genuine contradiction I can't resolve on my own:**
1. **Staging deploys:** one stored claim says *"merging to main deploys atlas to staging automatically,"* another says *"deploys to atlas staging are never automatic: someone runs `bin/ship.sh --staging` by hand."* These directly conflict and I have no way to tell which is current — which is it?
2. **"Feature flags" terminology:** one claim says *"feature flags in atlas are an environment variable map and nothing more,"* another says *"feature flags in atlas are additive only, so `cargo check --all-features` has to pass."* These read like they're describing two different mechanisms (runtime env-var flags vs. Cargo compile-time features) using the same term — is that right, or is one of these just wrong?
